# Retrospective audit — did endurance winners run fuel-limited?

The multi-stop model finds **180 of 205** planned race-seasons fuel-limited on stop count and **25 tyre-limited**, the latter concentrated entirely in the cheap-stop classes (see the [WEC](../wec/simulator_phase4.md) / [IMSA](../imsa/gtp/simulator_phase4.md) / [ELMS](../elms/simulator_phase4.md) reports).

This document once opened by saying *every* scoped race was fuel-limited. That was true of the prototype classes it was measured on and stated as a fact about endurance racing; [`when_tyres_beat_fuel.md`](when_tyres_beat_fuel.md) is what replaced it.

The audit below tests the model against **what the race winners actually did**: their real fuel-stint lengths, reconstructed from the committed laps and compared to each circuit's measured fuel range. No number is quoted from memory.

**178 of 209 audited winners ran fuel-limited** — at least one stint within 3 laps of the full fuel range, and a longest stint reaching it. Real winning behaviour corroborates the model's headline. **This exact share depends on that 3-lap tolerance** — see the [sensitivity sweep](fuel_limited_sensitivity.md), which reports it at every tolerance from 0 to 10 laps; the qualitative conclusion (a clear majority, in all three series) holds throughout, but the precise percentage should not be quoted alone — see [`fuel_limited_sensitivity.md`](fuel_limited_sensitivity.md) for the full sweep, including the per-series breakdown (IMSA moves more than WEC).

## Reading the exceptions

A winner whose longest stint falls short of the fuel range is not automatically a refutation: a race disrupted by many neutralisations bunches stops and shortens stints for reasons unrelated to tyres. Where a winner *does* run a full-range stint, though, it is direct evidence that the tank — not the tyre — set the stint length, exactly as the DP concluded from the degradation and pit-loss numbers independently.
